title: Make the SQL admin group the Entra admin of the PIM Manager database server
purpose: Make a role-assignable security group (default grp-pim-sql-admins) the Microsoft Entra admin of a PIM Manager environment's Azure SQL server, with the environment's managed identities, the nightly updater and the Invardia Support app as its members.
whenToRun: Once per environment when the install could not set up the SQL admin group itself (the installing identity did not hold the rights to create a role-assignable group), when PIM Manager or the updater reports that its identity cannot log in to the database, or when Invardia support needs access to the store. Safe to run again: a second run reports no changes.

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: The group is role-assignable (tier 0): only a Privileged Role Administrator or a Global Administrator can create such a group or change its members. Without it the group is not created and the current SQL admin is left as it is.

runAs.name: Contributor
runAs.scope: the Azure SQL server (or its resource group); Owner works too
runAs.why: Sets the server's Microsoft Entra admin (Microsoft.Sql/servers/administrators/write) and reads it back.

runAs.name: Reader
runAs.why: Finds the environment's user-assigned identities (id-pim-*) and the updater job's identity.

runAs.name: The person running it, signed in in the browser (or the Invardia Support app inside an Invardia support session)
runAs.why: The script takes its Microsoft Graph and Azure Resource Manager tokens from that sign-in (pinned to -TenantId) and refuses a token for another tenant. A certificate identity (-ClientId + -CertThumbprint) is for automation from the repository only; it then needs the Graph application permissions Group.Create and GroupMember.ReadWrite.All (or Group.ReadWrite.All), Directory.Read.All and RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory.

changes.object: security group grp-pim-sql-admins (or -GroupName), role-assignable (isAssignableToRole = true), only when it does not exist
changes.why: One group as the SQL admin means every identity that must administer the store gets access by membership, without a database login created by hand. Role-assignable so that a Groups Administrator, a User Administrator or a group owner cannot add themselves to it.
changes.undo: Delete the group in the Entra admin center (Groups) -- only after another Microsoft Entra admin has been set on the SQL server, or nobody can administer the database.

changes.object: member of grp-pim-sql-admins: the environment identity (id-pim-<token>), the SQL identity (id-pim-sql-<token>, private SQL only), the nightly updater's identity (ca-pim-update), the Invardia Support app (-SupportAppId / -SupportObjectId), every -ExtraMemberObjectIds, and the previous SQL admin (kept, so nobody loses access)
changes.permission: group member of the SQL server's Microsoft Entra admin group = administrator of the SQL server and every database on it
changes.why: The updater checks the database schema before it rolls a release, the Manager and engine read and write the store, and Invardia support needs access to the store to help.
changes.undo: Remove the member from the group (Entra admin center > Groups > grp-pim-sql-admins > Members). Removing the PIM identities stops PIM Manager.

changes.object: Microsoft Entra admin of the Azure SQL server (Microsoft.Sql/servers/administrators/ActiveDirectory) set to the group
changes.scope: the Azure SQL server named with -SqlServerName
changes.why: Azure SQL allows exactly one Microsoft Entra admin; making it the group gives every member access. Entra-only authentication is not changed (only read before and after). Existing contained database users are not touched.
changes.undo: Set the previous admin back (the script prints it): Azure portal > the SQL server > Microsoft Entra ID > Set admin.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The subscription of the environment (always named explicitly; never a default context).

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The environment's resource group (where its identities and the updater job are).

parameters.name: SqlServerName
parameters.help: The Azure SQL server name or FQDN.

parameters.name: SqlResourceGroup
parameters.help: The resource group of the SQL server when it is not the environment's.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id; every token is checked against it.

parameters.name: GroupObjectId
parameters.help: Use this existing group (object id) instead of looking it up by name.

parameters.name: EnvironmentIdentityName
parameters.default: the one id-pim-* identity in the resource group
parameters.help: The environment's user-assigned identity, when there is more than one candidate.

parameters.name: SqlAdminIdentityName
parameters.default: the one id-pim-sql-* identity in the resource group

parameters.name: UpdateJobName
parameters.help: The nightly updater job whose system-assigned identity becomes a member.

parameters.name: SupportAppId
parameters.help: The Invardia Support app's application id; its service principal becomes a member. The old name -TroubleshootingAppId still works.

parameters.name: SupportObjectId
parameters.help: The Invardia Support app's service principal object id, instead of -SupportAppId. The old name -TroubleshootingObjectId still works.

parameters.name: ExtraMemberObjectIds
parameters.help: More object ids to make members.

parameters.name: ClientId
parameters.help: Automation from the repository only: with -CertThumbprint, a certificate identity instead of the browser sign-in.

parameters.name: CertThumbprint
parameters.help: Automation from the repository only: the certificate (local store) of -ClientId.

parameters.name: MembersOnly
parameters.help: Only add the members, and only when the group already is the server's admin; never create the group or move the admin.

parameters.name: DoNotKeepCurrentAdmin
parameters.help: Do not make the current SQL admin a member of the group.

parameters.name: PlanOnly
parameters.help: Read everything and print the plan; change nothing (as -WhatIf).

readsOnly: the group (by name or id), whether it is a security group and role-assignable, and its members
the SQL server's current Microsoft Entra admin and its Entra-only authentication setting
the user-assigned identities in the resource group and the updater job's identity
the Invardia Support app's service principal (by application id)
network: localhost (the browser returns the sign-in to a local port on this computer)
whatIf: Signs in and reads everything, prints the plan, then one "What if:" line per change it would make: create the role-assignable group, add each member (by name and object id), make the group the SQL server's Microsoft Entra admin (and who the admin was). Nothing is created or changed.
undo: Set the previous Microsoft Entra admin back on the SQL server, then remove the members the script added (or delete the group if the script created it). Nothing else is changed by the script.
